challengesAndResolutions.topic: Comic economy and the offer's wrist turn
challengesAndResolutions.partnerFinding: A leaves the single offer versus wrist-flick question to continuous inspection and keeps the original peek comparison open.

Likewise, the one-peek definition is unchanged, so this successful gesture pass cannot promote the simpler edit as a better joke. A small drowsy-looking isolated endpoint also cannot reject the concealed-to-revealed sequence.
challengesAndResolutions.resolution: Keep continuous rhythm unscored and both peek versions available. Ask normal-speed playback the specific questions of whether the 2350–2720 ms turn reads as an offer and whether the second peek adds meaning. Use decoded frames to diagnose an observed issue, not to invent a result.

process: Carry each prior deduction into the next review with a matched before/current view and an explicit improved, corrected, unchanged or unmeasured disposition.

Use choreograph to cast attention as gaze lead/head support, then require that adaptive channels release for the authored visitor return before the offer. Keep question, layout and free hand quiet when they do not carry the current beat.
Inspect the full preparation/return/turn/hold and its endpoint at actual sizes. Separate useful contact from accidental contour congestion; do not use a universal rule that all hands must separate.

Use review-animations for purposeful input feedback and interruption checks, while retaining the deliberate multi-second character thought. Test the displayed pose handoff, not only the underlying raw engine state.

Use actual DOM scenes for spatial storytelling, first-viewport captures for exposure, and simplified comparison films for controlled pose differences. State exactly which kind of evidence supports each claim.

Use normal-speed playback for whether the offer feels like a small invitation or a wrist flick and whether a repeated peek adds meaning. Use frames and source to diagnose the specific failed moment. Keep precise shared vocabulary from becoming a quality claim.
exceptions: Do not compress intentional character content to the short UI feedback budget.
Do not remove keyboard Play to satisfy a no-keyboard-animation heuristic.
Do not replace expressive SVG anatomy with compositor-only shapes without a measured relevant workload.
Do not demand identical attention direction for different subject positions; preserve shared anatomy and exact per-composition day/night numeric parity instead.
Do not automatically delete a repeated peek, add a wave, enlarge mittens or break a deliberate clasp to create a more obvious isolated still.
Do not apply a website hero redesign workflow to erase the local study controls during this bounded gesture review.
